title: Bible: Life in New Testament Times

questions.question: Which three patriarchs are connected with the Abrahamic covenant in the notes?
questions.explanation: The notes connect the Abrahamic covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

questions.question: Where were the Israelites held captive before the conquest of the Promised Land?
questions.explanation: Egyptian captivity comes before the conquest of the Promised Land in the notes.

questions.question: Which sequence matches the early history outlined in the notes?
choices: Jewish self-rule, Egyptian captivity, conquest of the Promised Land
Conquest of the Promised Land, Jewish self-rule, Egyptian captivity
Egyptian captivity, conquest of the Promised Land, Jewish self-rule
Egyptian captivity, Jewish self-rule, conquest of the Promised Land
questions.explanation: The outline places captivity first, then conquest, and then self-rule.

questions.question: Which kings ruled Israel's united kingdom in the order listed?
questions.explanation: The notes list Saul, then David, then Solomon.

questions.question: After the kingdom divided, which kingdom was in the north?
questions.explanation: The notes place Israel in the north and Judah in the south.

questions.question: Which kingdom lay south of Israel after the kingdom divided?
questions.explanation: Judah was the southern kingdom in the divided-kingdom outline.

questions.question: Which empire conquered the northern kingdom of Israel?
questions.explanation: The historical outline identifies Assyria as the conqueror of northern Israel.

questions.question: What does it mean that Judah became a vassal state under Assyria?
choices: Judah became part of Egypt's royal family
Judah was subject to Assyrian authority
questions.explanation: A vassal state is subordinate to a stronger power; the notes describe Judah this way under Assyria.

questions.question: Which empire conquered Babylon, according to the outline?
questions.explanation: The notes say Persia conquered Babylon.

questions.question: Which sequence matches the later empires in the notes?
questions.explanation: The outline moves from Babylonian captivity through Persian and Greek rule to Roman rule.

questions.question: According to the notes, where did more Jews live during the Roman period?
questions.explanation: The notes state that more Jews lived outside Israel than inside it.

questions.question: Which religious concession did Rome make to the Jews in the notes?
choices: They could no longer offer Temple sacrifices
They had to pay taxes only to the Temple
They could choose the Roman emperor
They did not have to celebrate pagan rituals
questions.explanation: The notes list exemption from pagan rituals among Rome's concessions to the Jews.

questions.question: Where were Jews allowed to offer sacrifices under the arrangement described?
questions.explanation: The notes say Jews were allowed to offer sacrifices at the Temple.

questions.question: Which institution was allowed to collect the Temple tax from Jewish men across the empire?
questions.explanation: The continuation at the top of 7023 says the Temple could collect its tax from Jewish men in the empire.

questions.question: Which covenant is described as the seed of the Jewish faith?
questions.explanation: The notes call Abraham's covenant the seed of the Jewish faith.

questions.question: What does the outline connect with the giving of the Law?
choices: The Roman Senate and its roads
The Pax Romana and its taxes
questions.explanation: The notes connect the giving of the Law with the Ten Commandments and Deuteronomy.

questions.question: What does the term Diaspora describe in these notes?
choices: Jews scattered from Israel and resettled in other lands
The division of Israel into farming districts
The collection of the Temple tax
questions.explanation: Diaspora refers to the scattering and resettlement of Jews outside Israel.

questions.question: What role did synagogues serve in Jewish communities?
questions.explanation: The notes describe synagogues as centers of Jewish religious life.

questions.question: After Jews returned to Israel, what political condition does the outline describe?
choices: They ruled the whole Roman Empire
They never again faced foreign rule
They remained under various outside authorities
They immediately restored the united kingdom
questions.explanation: The notes say Jews returned under various political authorities and still were not free.

questions.question: Which ruler is identified as the king during the period discussed around Jesus' birth?
questions.explanation: The first-century section focuses on King Herod the Great.

questions.question: Who put Herod the Great in power, according to the notes?
choices: The kings of the united kingdom
questions.explanation: The notes describe Herod as a vassal king installed by the Roman Senate.

questions.question: Which Jerusalem structure did Herod especially expand and improve?
choices: The palace of Solomon in Egypt
questions.explanation: The notes emphasize Herod's expansion and improvement of Jerusalem, especially the Temple.

questions.question: In the biblical account summarized in the notes, why did Herod order the killing of young boys in Bethlehem?
choices: He was collecting the Temple tax
He was attempting to kill Jesus
questions.explanation: The notes connect the killings in Bethlehem with Herod's attempt to kill Jesus.

questions.question: What kind of Messiah were people expecting in the notes?
choices: A Roman tax collector who would increase taxes
An Assyrian king who would destroy Judah
A farmer who would stop all travel
A human military rescuer who would free them from oppressors
questions.explanation: The notes describe an expectation of a military Messiah who would rescue the people and restore a golden age.

questions.question: What does Pax Romana mean?
questions.explanation: The notes translate Pax Romana as Roman Peace.

questions.question: How did travel and trade change during the Pax Romana in the notes?
choices: They were limited to the city of Rome
They were limited to military supplies
questions.explanation: The economics section links the Pax Romana with a large increase in travel and trade.

questions.question: Why would greater political peace help travel and trade?
choices: Peace reduced the demand for farm products
Peace removed the need to move goods
More stable conditions made movement and exchange easier
Peace meant every village produced everything it needed
questions.explanation: This is an application of the notes' connection between political peace and increased travel and trade.

questions.question: What was the main economic activity described for the population?
questions.explanation: The notes describe an agrarian economy, centered on farming.

questions.question: What is a subsistence farmer?
choices: A farmer who produces just enough to get by
A ruler who collects taxes from farmers
A merchant who buys all food from abroad
A landowner who grows only luxury exports
questions.explanation: The notes explain subsistence farming as producing just enough to get by.

questions.question: Which group contains grains listed in the notes?
questions.explanation: Wheat, barley, millet, and rice appear in the grain list.

questions.question: Which group contains fruits listed in the notes?
questions.explanation: The notes list olives, figs, dates, and grapes as fruits.

questions.question: Which pair is listed as legumes?
questions.explanation: Lentils and beans are the legumes listed in the notes.

questions.question: Which group is listed with spices and seasonings?
questions.explanation: The notes group salt, pepper, and ginger under spices.

questions.question: Which meat in the notes is specifically marked as a Gentile food?
questions.explanation: The meat list marks pigs as Gentile food, distinguishing pork from the other listed foods.

questions.question: Which group is listed among the landowning elite?
questions.explanation: The notes place royal families among the landowning elite.

questions.question: Besides royal families, who is listed among the elite?
questions.explanation: Religious leaders and priests are the other group listed under the elite.

questions.question: Which group belongs to the peasantry in the notes?
questions.explanation: The notes include small landowners, tenant farmers, and wage laborers in the peasantry.

questions.question: How does a wage laborer earn a living?
choices: By collecting rent on all village farmland
By working in return for pay
By receiving tribute as a royal ruler
By collecting the Temple tax as a priest
questions.explanation: A wage laborer works for wages; this explains one of the groups in the notes' peasantry list.

questions.question: Which kind of trade supplied most of Judea's trade in the notes?
questions.explanation: The trade section says most trade was internal to Judea.

questions.question: Why did subsistence farming limit the ability to buy extra goods?
choices: Farmers spent all their money on foreign travel
All extra money went into building roads
Farmers could buy goods only from the Senate
People had little or no money left for amenities
questions.explanation: The notes say people had little or no extra money to spend on amenities.

questions.question: Why did having few surplus products limit international trade?
choices: There was little extra produce to sell abroad
Local farmers were required to export all grain
Overseas buyers accepted only luxury goods
The same products were never grown abroad
questions.explanation: The notes list little extra produce to sell abroad as a reason for limited international trade.

questions.question: What additional barrier to international trade is mentioned in the notes?
choices: A ban on every form of local exchange
A lack of demand for any food
questions.explanation: The notes list religious disinclination toward international commerce alongside limited money and surplus goods.

questions.question: Which oil is listed as an export?
questions.explanation: Olive oil appears in the export list at the top of 7026.

questions.question: Which fruit is listed as an export?
questions.explanation: Dates are named in the notes' export list.

questions.question: What was opobalsam, called the Balm of Gilead in the notes?
choices: A tax paid to the Roman Senate
questions.explanation: The notes describe opobalsam as an aromatic resinous juice from a shrub, called the Balm of Gilead.

questions.question: Why was Israel subject to Roman taxation?
choices: It was part of the Roman Empire
It collected taxes from Roman provinces
It had no local religious institutions
questions.explanation: The taxation section says Israel was taxed as part of the Roman Empire.

questions.question: About how much work did the annual Temple tax represent in the notes?
questions.explanation: The notes describe the Temple tax for each Jewish man as about two days' wages.

questions.question: What approximate total taxation rate do the notes give?
questions.explanation: The notes estimate total taxation at about 30 percent.

questions.question: Which group contains technological advances listed in the notes?
choices: Steam engines, railways, and steel mills
questions.explanation: The technology section lists cement, the water wheel, and millstones before discussing roads and arches.

questions.question: Where were roads more common, according to the notes?
questions.explanation: The notes describe roads as more common outside Israel.

questions.question: About how wide was an average Roman road in the notes?
questions.explanation: The notes give an average width of around 6 meters, approximately 20 feet.

questions.question: What military benefit did Roman roads provide?
choices: They replaced soldiers with tax collectors
They prevented travel between military bases
They limited armies to travel by sea
They improved the movement of military forces
questions.explanation: The notes connect roads with military advantage and identify military roads.

questions.question: How did Roman roads affect communication?
choices: It restricted messages to a single town
It required all messages to pass through Jerusalem
questions.explanation: The notes specifically say roads increased communication speed.

questions.question: What do the notes say about some Roman roads today?
choices: Every road was replaced by a canal
All are used only as military bases
questions.explanation: The technology section says some Roman roads are still used today.

questions.question: According to the notes, what did the Romans do with arches?
choices: Used them only in temporary tents
Restricted their use to farm tools
questions.explanation: The notes say arches were perfected by the Romans during this period.

questions.question: Which group lists uses of arches in the notes?
choices: Doorways and gates, bridges, and aqueducts
questions.explanation: The notes list buildings' doors and gates, bridges, and aqueducts as uses of arches.

questions.question: Which thinker is associated with calculating Earth's circumference in the notes?
questions.explanation: The notes associate Eratosthenes with recognizing Earth's shape and calculating its circumference; the questionable date is excluded.

questions.question: What field did the notes associate with Eratosthenes?
questions.explanation: The notes call Eratosthenes the Father of Geography.

questions.question: Which procedure is listed as something ancient doctors performed?
questions.explanation: The medicine section lists amputations, eye operations, and tracheotomies; it does not list modern procedures.

questions.question: Which material do the notes say was used for dental fillings?
questions.explanation: The dental-work section mentions fillings made with gold.

questions.question: How close to the actual value do the notes say Eratosthenes' calculation was?
questions.explanation: The notes say his calculation was within 1 percent of the actual value.

questions.question: What circumference of Earth is given in the notes?
questions.explanation: The notes describe Earth's circumference as 24,000 miles.

questions.question: According to the class notes, what did ancient doctors lack when performing operations?
questions.explanation: The notes say doctors performed operations but had no anesthetics.

questions.question: What sources of material for false teeth are listed in the notes?
questions.explanation: The notes say false teeth were made using animal and human teeth.

questions.question: How many years of silence from God before Jesus are described in the class notes?
questions.explanation: The notes describe 450 years of silence from God before the time of Jesus.

questions.question: What reason do the class notes give for creating synagogues in towns?
choices: The Roman Senate had moved to Judea
Herod had banned all religious gatherings
questions.explanation: The notes say synagogues were created in towns as centers of Jewish religion because the Temple had been destroyed.

questions.question: What share of the population do the notes identify as the elite?
questions.explanation: The notes place the landowning elite at 10 percent.

questions.question: What share of the population do the notes identify as the peasantry?
questions.explanation: The notes place the peasantry at 90 percent.

questions.question: What percentage of the Roman Empire's population do the class notes say was Jewish?
questions.explanation: The notes state that Jews made up 7 percent of the empire.

questions.question: During what years do the notes place Herod's expansion and improvement of the Temple?
questions.explanation: The notes give 20–16 BC for Herod's expansion and improvement of the Temple.

questions.question: Using the corrected class-note date, about when did Eratosthenes calculate Earth's circumference?
questions.explanation: The intended class-note date is about 200 BC, with the extra zero removed as requested.

questions.question: About how long did Egyptian captivity last in the class outline?
questions.explanation: The notes give approximately 400 years for Egyptian captivity.

questions.question: How long does the outline give for the conquest of the Promised Land?
questions.explanation: The notes give approximately seven years for the conquest of the Promised Land.

questions.question: About how long did Jewish self-rule last in the early historical outline?
questions.explanation: The outline places roughly 400 years of Jewish self-rule after the conquest.

questions.question: What dates do the notes give for Israel's united kingdom?
questions.explanation: The notes date the united kingdom from 1050 to 930 BC.

questions.question: How long did each of Saul, David, and Solomon reign, according to the notes?
questions.explanation: The notes give each of these three kings a reign of 40 years.

questions.question: When does the class outline place the beginning of the divided kingdom?
questions.explanation: The divided-kingdom section begins at 930 BC in the notes.

questions.question: What year does the outline give for Babylonian captivity?
questions.explanation: The notes place Babylonian captivity at 587 BC.

questions.question: What year do the notes give for Persia's conquest of Babylon?
questions.explanation: The notes say Persia conquered Babylon in 539 BC.

questions.question: What date is written beside the Greek Empire in the class outline?
questions.explanation: The class outline gives 329 BC for the Greek Empire.

questions.question: What date marks the beginning of Roman rule in the class outline?
questions.explanation: The notes give 63 BC beside the Roman Empire.

questions.question: When do the notes say Assyria made Judah a vassal state?
questions.explanation: The notes place Judah's vassal status under Assyria at 701 BC.

questions.question: Which group contains vegetables listed in the notes?
questions.explanation: The vegetable list includes onions, garlic, leeks, squash, cabbage, radishes, and beets.

questions.question: Who was required to pay the Temple tax in the notes?
choices: Only Jewish men living in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: The notes describe the Temple tax as applying to every Jewish man.

questions.question: Which period does the outline call the golden age of Israel?
questions.explanation: The notes label the united kingdom the golden age of Israel.

questions.question: Besides fillings and false teeth, what dental practice is mentioned in the notes?
questions.explanation: The dental-work section also mentions polishing teeth.
